keywords: n-base, numeral system 2.Floating point number 3.Sets and logic 4.Logical circuit 5.Organizing data and basic statistics
educationalGoal: Students will: (1) learn how to express n-base and floating point numbers (IEEE754). (2) apply the concept of sets to logical algebra and learn the basics of how to represent logic in a computer. Learn how to configure logic circuits to implement logic in a computer. (3) learn basic probabilities, conditional probabilities, and Bayes' theorem. Learn basic data organization and statistics using Excel.
advice: This is a basic course in mathematics, logic, and statistics. We will cover the following topics: 1. n-base: binary system, octal system, hexadecimal system. 2. Representation of numbers in computers: Floating point number (IEEE754). 3. Sets and Logic: basic set theory, propositional logic, truth table, logical circuit. 4. Basic probabilities: Permutations and combinations, probabilities, conditional probabilities and Bayes' theorem. 5: A data analysis method using statistics: Frequency distribution table, histogram, correlation diagram, mean/variance, covariance/correlation coefficient. Students are expected to understand above materials. Students are expected to process data using Excel (computer spreadsheet software). Students are expected to complete the exercises on their own without consulting/copying others. Students are expected to utilize the Math. and Science Education Research Center or the office hours of the teacher.
books: Textbooks: Mathematics for Information Science (Kanazawa Institute of Technology) Reference books: None Reserved books: None
requiredKnowledge: A background knowledge of integer arithmetic operations is required; students also need the ability to absorb and exercise new knowledge.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand radix conversion from decimal to n-base and calculate binary arithmetic operations.
Be able to understand the concept of sets and logics, the representation of numbers/logic in computers.
Be able to understand probabilities, conditional probabilities, and Bayes' theorem.
Be able to perform basic data processing using Excel.
Understand the meanings of fundamental english words for mathematics.
Be able to demonstrate an understanding of all class material, attend every class, and complete the handouts.

achievementLevels.ideal: Demonstrate a 90% achievement level in the following areas: (1) Understand relationship between decimal numbers and n-digit numbers accurately. (2) Understand the representation of binary fractions and be able to correctly transform to floating point numbers. (3) Correctly understand sets and logical operations. (4) Correctly calculate probabilities and conditional probabilities, and apply Bayes' theorem. (5) Understand the basics of statistics, accurately determine characteristic values of data, and create effective data visualizations.
achievementLevels.standard: Demonstrate a 60% achievement level in the following areas: (1) Understand relationship between decimal numbers and n-digit numbers. (2) Understand the representation of binary fractions and be able to transform to floating point numbers. (3) Understand set symbols and logical operations. (4) Calculate simple probabilities and conditional probabilities, and apply Bayes' theorem. (5) Understand the basics of statistics, determine characteristic values of data, and create effective data visualizations.
